title: Use Linux, GCC, and LLVM source patterns as language capability requirements
description: Inspect pinned Linux, GCC, LLVM, and Code of Honor source for intrusive lists, graph mutation, ownership, concurrency, callbacks, and layout. Record concrete capability witnesses. Replace the mandatory checked-pool direction with direct embedded links and explicit lifetime contracts, per user correction. Preserve the requirement for user-written list code without unsafe and C-level frontend speed; do not claim unproved memory safety. Use subagents for source research and design review.
close_reason: Inspected pinned Linux, GCC, LLVM, and Coho sources with subagents. Added source witnesses and revised the proposal around direct embedded links, independent ownership, and explicit lifetime requirements. Removed the mandatory pool direction. Verified document links and source ranges; safety and compilation-speed gates remain stated as unproved experiments.

title: Investigate Jai metacompilation and a small extensible language core
description: Investigate public Jai metacompilation, Lisp and Scheme/Racket, Forth and Factor, academic staging and extensible compiler work, and cache and parallel scheduling costs. Document a fully exposed compiler core and replaceable user stage setup, source-backed options, and falsifiable cold C-speed gates. Keep implementation expansion bounded by production witnesses.
close_reason: Recorded primary Jai, Lisp/Scheme/Racket, Forth/Factor, and academic evidence. Added full public compiler core and stage setup, concrete cache contracts, and cold compilation gates. Reviewed with three subagents and validated document links and formatting.

title: Find Walter Bright sources on parallel D compilation

close_reason: Found Walter Bright original 2009 parallel-compilation article, 2016 semantic-analysis caveat, and verified 2020/2023/2024 comments via the official HN API. Added dated primary sources and phase-separation conclusions to the design document. Distinguished implemented I/O overlap, proposed per-module lex/parse, and historical implementation status.

title: Explore a minimal systems language with C-level front-end speed
description: Research C, C++, D, Rust, Zig, public Jai, and academic work with subagents. Write a source-checked exploration and bounded language proposal. Make C-level front-end speed the primary gate. Include fast readable syntax, parallel compiler stages, and safe user-implemented intrusive doubly-linked lists. Define compilation/runtime gates and production witnesses. Documentation only; no compiler implementation.
close_reason: Completed the source-linked language and academic exploration, concrete ownership and checked intrusive-list design, syntax and parallel stage proposal, and measurable acceptance gates.

title: Measure frontend compilation costs in C, C++, and Rust
description: Profile installed compilers on pinned real source workloads. Exclude backend optimization and code emission. Record repeatable commands, process timing, disjoint phase attribution, source hashes, tool versions, and measurement limits. Add results to the language study.
close_reason: Measured 160 frontend checks, 24 phase profiles, and 4 sampling profiles for pinned C/C++/Rust workloads. Saved reproducible scripts, evidence, profiler-overhead analysis, source-checked boundaries, and design consequences. Validated data coverage, trace accounting, input checks, timeout cleanup, and repeat analysis.
